short: Speech synthesis from fused sEMG and lip video is new to the ledger (M05, ahead); span masking (M03) adds a non-significant clean gain; seen speakers only (M12, behind).
position: The paper [@delblanco2026xmask] changes the sensors (M05), synthesizing speech from fused surface EMG and lip video, and the training (M03), masking spans of each stream. The sensor pairing is ahead: both earlier fused sEMG-video decoders in the ledger classify words or sentences (Appendix), and here the pair cuts silent-speech WER from 54.5% (best lip-only model) to 40.5% for six laryngeal speakers (Table III). The masking is standard: span masking added to a video dropout of up to 75% (§IV-D), never compared with whole-stream dropout of both streams, with a clean gain of 3.5 points the authors call not statistically significant (§V-B). The strongest confound is capacity: with sEMG zeroed at test, the unmasked multimodal model still reaches 46.9% WER, so 7.6 of its 10.5-point lead over lip-only needs no sEMG (inference). The evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: test speakers are all seen in training (Table I), with no listener test or repeated runs, and for three laryngectomized speakers the gain is not significant (§V-E).
